comparator.name: Astronomy
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define a mandatory 150-EC Astronomy major and a 30-EC free minor. The pathway below accounts for the complete 180 EC and preserves the genuine 30-EC minor space rather than silently selecting either of the two optional deepening minors or inventing an unrelated minor. The Astronomy and Astronomy Instrumentation and Informatics deepening minors are available choices, not formally distinct routes through the bachelor; no formal route is therefore assigned.
components: Introduction to Programming and Computational Methods
Genuine 30-EC free minor space preserved from the official curriculum.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and dynamical-system modelling for scientific questions
Programming, algorithms, databases, scientific data, image analysis and machine learning
Observation, satellite imagery, signals, robotics, autonomous systems and computational instrumentation
Research design, statistical inference and ethical reflection for computational scientific work

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, scientific data & autonomous systems
alternatives.concept: Develop mathematics, numerical modelling, programming, algorithms, databases, statistics, image analysis, machine learning, signals, satellite observation and computational autonomy. This is a related response to the target’s modelling, astronomical-data and instrumentation directions, not an Astronomy or Astrophysics substitute.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is dominated by mathematics, computing, data analysis, imaging, signals and autonomous systems, with one satellite-observation application. The label deliberately does not claim astronomy, astrophysics, cosmology or planetary science content.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, four per fixed semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and six level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned term. Programming precedes algorithms, AI planning and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics, neural networks and robotics; Sustainability Essentials I precedes Earth Observation.

candidates.label: Astrophysics, cosmology, galaxies, stars and planetary systems
Radio astronomy and experimental astronomical observation

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the evidence, relevance and mechanical gates. It responds to the target’s mathematical modelling, computational analysis, observation-data and instrumentation/informatics directions through actual mathematics, programming, databases, algorithms, statistics, imaging, signals, robotics, satellite observation and autonomous-system content. It is explicitly not presented as Astronomy. A disciplinary astrophysics route cannot supply mechanics, electromagnetism, waves and optics, quantum or thermal physics, stellar and galactic physics, cosmology, radiative processes, hydrodynamics or planetary science. A radio-astronomy and experimental-observation route cannot supply telescopes, radio instrumentation, physical measurement laboratories or astronomy field methods. No padded second programme is produced.

blocks: Both establish calculus and mathematical techniques for later scientific work; UCR is a general mathematics foundation rather than physics-specific training.
Both directly study vectors, matrices, systems of equations and linear transformations.
Both develop numerical methods for scientific equations and models; UCR is not astronomy-specific.
Both extend calculus for scientific analysis; the external course is embedded in the physics progression.
Both use differential equations to analyse systems; UCR additionally emphasises signals, state-space and control representations.
Both develop probability and statistical inference for uncertain data; UCR is general rather than astronomy-specific.
Both establish programming and computational problem-solving; the external component applies these methods within Astronomy.
Both use instrument-derived observations and image data; UCR focuses satellite and drone observation of Earth and does not teach telescopes or astronomical observing.

notes.text: The UCR programme combines mathematics, scientific computing, databases, image and data analysis, signals, satellite observation, robotics and autonomous-system methods. It does not reproduce the target’s mechanics, electromagnetism, waves and optics, quantum and thermal physics, astronomy, astrophysics, cosmology, planetary science, observational or experimental-physics laboratories, or discipline-specific research project.
